questions.question: What should every one of these projects include before styling?
questions.answer: A valid document shell (doctype, lang, charset, viewport, title), semantic landmarks, labeled controls, image alt and dimensions, and a logical heading outline. Verify with the validator, keyboard tabbing, and a no-CSS pass.

questions.question: Which elements make the profile page semantic rather than div soup?
questions.answer: header with h1 and nav, main with article and section, address for contact, and footer. Image has alt and dimensions; sections are named with aria-labelledby.

questions.question: What makes the signup form accessible?
questions.answer: Every control has a label tied by for/id, related fields sit in a fieldset with a legend, autocomplete tokens are set, validation attributes are native, helper text is linked with aria-describedby, and the button declares type=submit.

questions.question: Which table features does the pricing build demonstrate?
questions.answer: caption for the table name, thead/tbody/tfoot grouping, th with scope=col/row, colspan for the footer row, and a scroll wrapper for narrow screens without destroying table semantics.

questions.question: Why should you test a project with CSS disabled before calling it done?
questions.answer: It exposes whether the document order, headings, labels, and links still make sense without visual layout. If the page is unusable without CSS, the HTML structure or semantics are incomplete.

questions.question: A project looks perfect but fails keyboard testing. What are the usual causes?
questions.answer: Clickable divs instead of buttons/links, missing focus styles, positive tabindex, hidden focusable elements (aria-hidden), or custom widgets without keyboard handlers. Use native elements and verify tab order.
